text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The consultative council will discuss in the next few days the federal budget and investment plan for the 1997/2002 five year plan, in which an increase in productivity of 24.9 billion pounds is seen in the first year. The private sector is seen contributing to more than 70 percent of the gross domestic product. Jobs for 540,000 people will be created.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa returned to Cairo from Uganda and said that he will give President Hosni Mubarak a complete report of his tour in Africa which also included Kenya, Djibouti, and Tanzania.
- Reporters Without Borders report says that journalists work freely in Egypt under the leadership of Mubarak.
- Parliament agrees in principle to an investment guarantee law.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will visit Cairo today to discuss ways of getting the peace process moving.
- Mubarak and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khalifa bin Zaid al-Nahayan met in the Egyptian resort of Sharm el-Sheikh.
- Pensions to rise to at least 800 pounds per month from July.
- Work is continuing on the Sheikh Zaid irrigation channel at Toshka and workers hope to shorten the time it takes to dig the project to 24 months from 30 as a birthday gift to Mubarak.

- Ramses statue which now stands at the station will be moved to its original place in the Giza governorate, says the committee charged with moving the Cairo landmark. The suggestion to move it to Cairo Opera House complex was rejected.
